cards.head: Deep caries: stop short of the pulp, fail less often
cards.take: A Cochrane network meta-analysis pooled 27 trials (3350 people, 4195 teeth). In deep lesions of permanent teeth, complete removal to hard dentine failed more often than stepwise excavation (OR 2.06) and far more than selective removal leaving soft dentine over the pulp (OR 11.32, wide CI). Most trials had high risk of bias. Chairside: clear the periphery fully, leave leathery dentine pulpally, seal well.
cards.rib: Leave soft dentine over the pulp, but seal the margins well

fig.title: Deep lesions, permanent teeth: odds of failure

cards.head: Posterior composites fail about twice as often as amalgam
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 8 trials (mostly children) found composite fillings in back teeth failed more often than amalgam (RR 1.89) and developed more secondary caries (RR 2.14); fracture rates were similar. Evidence certainty was low and the trials are old. Chairside: if you place posterior composites, isolate well and manage caries risk, and discuss longevity honestly with the patient.
cards.rib: Isolate well and control caries risk when placing composites

cards.head: Fluoride varnish cuts caries by about 40% in children
cards.take: This Cochrane review pooled 22 trials with 12,455 children. Fluoride varnish applied two to four times a year reduced decayed, missing and filled surfaces by 43% in permanent teeth and by 37% in primary teeth compared with placebo or no treatment. Evidence quality was moderate. Chairside: varnish takes a minute, needs no special cooperation and suits every child at raised caries risk.
cards.rib: Apply fluoride varnish 2-4 times a year in at-risk children

cards.head: Hall crowns beat usual fillings in primary molars
cards.take: In a Scottish practice-based trial of 132 children, one carious primary molar got a preformed metal crown cemented without drilling or local anaesthetic (Hall technique) and the other got the dentist's usual filling. At 5 years, major failures (pain, abscess, pulpitis) were 3% with Hall crowns versus 16.5% with fillings. Chairside: for an asymptomatic carious primary molar, Hall crowns are a quick, well-tolerated option.
cards.rib: Seal asymptomatic carious primary molars under a Hall crown

cards.ev: Network meta-analysis · J Oral Pathol Med 2023
cards.head: Aphthous ulcers: no topical gel clearly wins on pain
cards.take: A network meta-analysis compared 20 topical medicines for recurrent aphthous stomatitis across 43 randomised trials (3067 people). None was clearly better than the others for pain, with low-to-moderate certainty evidence; topical doxycycline ranked best for speeding healing. Chairside: choose a cheap, safe topical, start it early in the ulcer cycle, and look for triggers such as trauma, deficiency or systemic disease in frequent cases.
cards.rib: Start a simple topical early and look for causes in frequent cases

cards.head: Denture stomatitis: topical antifungal plus denture care
cards.take: A network meta-analysis of 25 studies ranked treatments for denture stomatitis. Topical antifungals gave the most clinical improvement (RR 4.37 vs control), and microwave disinfection of the denture plus a topical antifungal gave the best Candida clearance (RR 7.38). Confidence in the evidence was low. Chairside: prescribe a topical antifungal and treat the denture too, with nightly removal and cleaning.
cards.rib: Treat the denture as well as the palate, and remove it at night

cards.head: Routine CBCT before third molar removal adds little
cards.take: In a multicentre trial, 256 patients having lower wisdom teeth removed were randomised to planning with CBCT or a panoramic radiograph. Nerve numbness at 7 days was 1.5% after CBCT and 3.8% after panoramic planning, a difference that was not significant, and CBCT did not reduce complications. Chairside: start with a good OPG; keep CBCT for cases where the root clearly overlaps the canal.
cards.rib: Start with an OPG; keep CBCT for close root-canal relations

cards.head: AI on bitewings helps dentists spot more caries
cards.take: In a randomised crossover trial, 22 dentists read bitewing radiographs with or without an AI caries-detection aid. With AI, sensitivity rose from 0.72 to 0.81 and overall accuracy (AUC) from 0.85 to 0.89, with no significant loss of specificity. But dentists using AI also chose more invasive treatment. Chairside: treat AI marks as a second opinion; an enamel shadow still deserves prevention, not a drill.
cards.rib: Use AI marks as a second look; keep enamel lesions non-invasive

cards.head: Rectangular collimation cuts intraoral X-ray dose sharply
cards.take: A systematic review of 13 studies found that switching from a round to a rectangular collimator reduced patient radiation dose by 40% to 92% for intraoral radiographs, with moderate-quality evidence. Retakes may rise briefly while staff learn to align it. Chairside: fit a rectangular collimator on every intraoral unit, use holders for alignment and the fastest receptor, especially for children.
cards.rib: Fit a rectangular collimator and use film holders for alignment

cards.head: Lead aprons and thyroid collars no longer advised
cards.take: The American Academy of Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology reviewed dose studies and advised stopping gonadal, pelvic and fetal shielding for all dental radiographs, and not using thyroid collars for intraoral, panoramic, cephalometric or CBCT imaging. Modern beams expose these organs very little, and shields can block the view and cause retakes. Chairside: protect patients through justified images, rectangular collimation and fast receptors instead.
cards.rib: Protect with justification, collimation and fast receptors instead

cards.ev: Systematic review & meta-analysis · Int J Prosthodont 2026
cards.head: Monolithic ceramic crowns now match metal-ceramic
cards.take: This meta-analysis of 64 studies (over 11,500 single crowns) found 5-year survival of 98.5% for monolithic lithium disilicate, 96.8% for monolithic zirconia and 97.1% for metal-ceramic crowns. Feldspathic ceramic crowns did worst at 90.4%. Monolithic designs reduced chipping and fracture. Chairside: for a single crown, a monolithic lithium disilicate or zirconia crown is a reliable metal-free choice.
cards.rib: Choose a monolithic design to avoid veneer chipping

cards.head: Lost molars: shortened arch does as well as a partial
cards.take: In a German multicentre trial, 152 patients missing all molars in one jaw got either a partial denture replacing the molars or a shortened dental arch ending at the premolars. After 5 years, survival free of further tooth loss was 0.74 in both groups. Chairside: when premolars are sound, a shortened arch is a valid, cheaper plan without a denture.
cards.rib: Offer a shortened arch when premolars are healthy and stable

cards.head: Scaling and root planing lowers HbA1c in diabetes
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 35 trials (3249 people with diabetes and periodontitis) found that subgingival instrumentation lowered HbA1c by 0.43 percentage points at 3-4 months and by 0.30 at 6 months compared with no treatment or usual care. The evidence was moderate certainty and further trials are unlikely to change it. Chairside: treat diabetic patients' periodontitis and tell their physician it helps.
cards.rib: Screen diabetic patients' gums and treat periodontitis early

cards.ev: Population attributable fraction study · Lancet Oncol 2024
cards.head: One in three oral cancers comes from chewing
cards.take: IARC researchers estimated that over 120,000 oral cancers worldwide in 2022, one third of all cases, were caused by smokeless tobacco and areca nut. India alone accounted for 83,400 of them and Bangladesh for 9,700; 77% were in men. Areca nut itself is largely unregulated. Chairside: ask every patient about gutkha, khaini, paan and plain supari, and record it like a vital sign.
cards.rib: Ask every patient about tobacco, paan and plain supari use

cards.head: Dentists can help patients quit tobacco
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 20 trials (14,897 people) tested quit support given in dental settings. Even a single session of behavioural support roughly doubled long-term abstinence (RR 1.86, very low certainty). Support plus nicotine replacement raised quit rates to 74 per 1000, against 27 per 1000 without support (moderate certainty). Chairside: ask, advise and offer help at every visit, and add nicotine replacement for smokers.
cards.rib: Ask, advise and offer quit help at every single visit

cards.head: Stains and lights cannot replace a biopsy
cards.take: This Cochrane review pooled 63 studies of 7942 suspicious mouth lesions. Vital staining (such as toluidine blue) caught 86% of cancers and dysplasias but was specific only 68% of the time; light-based devices 87% and 50%. Brush cytology did best at 90% and 94%. No adjunct can replace a scalpel biopsy. Chairside: a suspicious lesion goes for biopsy, whatever a stain or light shows.
cards.rib: Biopsy every suspicious lesion, whatever the stain or light shows

cards.head: No pill or gel is proven to stop leukoplakia turning
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 14 trials (909 people) tested vitamin A, beta carotene, lycopene, bleomycin and other treatments for oral leukoplakia. Some healed lesions for a while, but relapse was common and none reduced cancer risk compared with placebo over 2 to 7 years. No trial has tested surgery against no treatment. Chairside: rely on biopsy, habit cessation and lifelong review, not on supplements.
cards.rib: Rely on biopsy, habit cessation and review, not supplements

cards.head: Irradiated jaw: save the tooth, and plan any extraction
cards.take: The 2024 ISOO-MASCC-ASCO guideline flags jaw doses of 50 Gy or more as the osteoradionecrosis risk zone. After radiotherapy, prefer root canal treatment, fillings or crowns over extraction in high-risk areas. If extraction is unavoidable, check the radiation plan, consider antibiotics and pentoxifylline-tocopherol, and use chlorhexidine rinses. Daily prescription fluoride (strong recommendation) prevents the caries that lead to extractions.
cards.rib: Check the jaw dose map before extracting after radiotherapy

cards.head: Low-level laser helps prevent radiation mouth sores
cards.take: The MASCC/ISOO systematic review and guideline recommends intraoral photobiomodulation (low-level laser) to prevent oral mucositis and its pain in head and neck radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy, and in stem cell transplant. Benefit depends on following a tested protocol exactly, for example 632.8 nm at 3 J/cm2, five days a week through radiotherapy. Chairside: if you have a suitable laser, coordinate with the oncology team.
cards.rib: Offer protocol-based laser therapy during head-neck radiotherapy

cards.ev: WHO Collaborating Centre consensus · Oral Dis 2021
cards.head: WHO's 2020 list of potentially malignant disorders
cards.take: An international WHO Collaborating Centre seminar updated the list of oral potentially malignant disorders. Most entities stayed. Oral lichenoid lesions and oral chronic graft-versus-host disease were added; chronic hyperplastic candidosis and verrucous hyperplasia were dropped for lack of evidence, and epidermolysis bullosa was moved to limited evidence. Chairside: a lichenoid lesion next to a restoration or drug history also needs follow-up.
cards.rib: Keep lichenoid lesions on your recall list, not just leukoplakia

cards.head: Trained health workers can spot oral lesions well
cards.take: This meta-analysis pooled 5 studies with 10,069 people screened by trained frontline health workers using a simple visual mouth examination. They picked up oral cancers and potentially malignant disorders with 88.8% sensitivity and 91.9% specificity. No eligible studies tested stains, cytology or lights for mass screening. Chairside: a careful look with good light, done by a trained person, is the screening tool that works.
cards.rib: Train your staff to look, and refer every positive screen

cards.head: Phone photos plus a remote specialist catch most lesions
cards.take: In an Indian multicentre study, 5025 people were screened by frontline workers who photographed the mouth with a phone-based device. Remote specialists reading the images agreed with on-site specialists with 95% sensitivity and 84% specificity, whereas workers judging by eye alone reached only 60% sensitivity. Chairside: clear intraoral photos sent to an oral specialist are a reliable way to triage a doubtful lesion.
cards.rib: Send clear intraoral photos to a specialist when unsure

cards.ev: Systematic review & meta-analysis · Front Public Health 2023
cards.head: Oral cancer patients wait about 7 weeks before seeking help
cards.take: This meta-analysis of 28 studies (30,845 patients) timed each step of the oral cancer pathway. The median wait from first symptom to first visit was 47 days, then 35 days from first visit to diagnosis and 30 days from diagnosis to treatment. Longer waits were shaped by social and economic context and may worsen survival. Chairside: arrange biopsy or referral that week.
cards.rib: Book the biopsy or referral the same week you see the lesion

fig.title: Median intervals on the oral cancer pathway

cards.head: Helping gutkha and khaini users quit: what works
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 34 trials (over 16,000 smokeless tobacco users) found varenicline raised quit rates (RR 1.34), as did nicotine lozenges (RR 1.36, low confidence). Nicotine patches, gum and bupropion showed no clear benefit. Most behavioural programmes helped, though effect sizes varied. Chairside: give clear quit advice and a follow-up date, and refer heavy chewers to a cessation clinic for medication.
cards.rib: Advise quitting, set a date and refer heavy chewers for medicine

cards.head: Floss or interdental brushes add a little to brushing
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 35 trials (3929 adults) found that adding floss or interdental brushes to toothbrushing may reduce gingivitis and plaque in the short term, and interdental brushes may work better than floss. Evidence for wooden sticks and water flossers was limited and inconsistent; certainty was low to very low. Chairside: size and demonstrate an interdental brush for open spaces; floss tight contacts.
cards.rib: Size and demonstrate an interdental brush for open contacts

cards.head: Full pulpotomy matches root canal in painful vital molars
cards.take: In a randomised trial of 160 mature molars with irreversible pulpitis, full pulpotomy with a calcium silicate cement was compared with root canal treatment. At 12 months clinical success was 97.3% vs 98.6% and radiographic success 93.3% vs 94.6%, while pain fell faster on day 1 after pulpotomy. Follow-up is short. Chairside: when bleeding stops after pulp removal, full pulpotomy is a quicker, cheaper option.
cards.rib: Offer full pulpotomy when coronal pulp bleeding can be controlled

cards.head: No retainer type is clearly best after braces
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 47 studies (4377 patients) compared fixed and removable retainers. Differences in lower incisor alignment were under 1 mm, too small to matter clinically. Clear plastic retainers failed less often than Hawley retainers (RR 0.60) and were more comfortable. Evidence was low to very low certainty. Chairside: pick a retainer the patient will actually wear, and plan long-term retention checks.
cards.rib: Choose the retainer the patient will wear, and review it yearly

cards.ev: Systematic review of RCTs · Int J Oral Implantol 2019
cards.head: Short implants can spare the posterior mandible a graft
cards.take: This review pooled 4 randomised trials (135 patients) comparing short implants with longer implants placed after vertical bone augmentation in atrophic posterior mandibles. At 5 years implant and prosthesis failures were similar, but the graft route had far more complications (RR 4.72) and 0.6 mm more bone loss. Chairside: with limited height above the canal, consider short implants before referring for vertical augmentation.
cards.rib: Consider short implants before planning a vertical bone graft

cards.head: Smokers' implants fail more than twice as often
cards.take: This meta-analysis of 292 publications covered over 150,000 implants. Implants in smokers had 2.4 times the odds of failure of those in non-smokers (OR 2.402), in both jaws, and lost 0.58 mm more marginal bone. The effect did not fade with longer follow-up. Most studies were retrospective. Chairside: document smoking before implant planning, warn about the risk, and offer quit support well before surgery.
cards.rib: Record smoking and offer quit support before planning implants

cards.head: Chlorhexidine roughly halves dry socket risk
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 49 trials found that chlorhexidine rinse (0.12% or 0.2%) or 0.2% chlorhexidine gel placed in the socket probably reduces dry socket, with odds ratios of 0.38 and 0.44 (moderate certainty). Benefit depends on baseline risk: about 7 surgical third molars treated prevent one dry socket, but 162 simple extractions. Chairside: use chlorhexidine for surgical third molars and other high-risk extractions.
cards.rib: Use chlorhexidine around surgical third molar removal

fig.title: Number needed to treat to prevent one dry socket

cards.ev: Systematic review & meta-analysis · Int J Oral Maxillofac Surg 2019
cards.head: Submucosal dexamethasone eases pain and swelling
cards.take: This meta-analysis of 17 randomised trials found that a submucosal dexamethasone injection at lower third molar surgery reduced early pain and swelling: about 4 patients treated spares one from early pain, and 5 from early oedema. The effect on mouth opening was under 5 mm and not clinically important. Evidence was low to moderate quality. Chairside: consider submucosal dexamethasone for difficult surgical third molars.
cards.rib: Consider submucosal dexamethasone for difficult third molars

fig.title: Submucosal dexamethasone: number needed to treat

cards.head: About 1 in 8 children has molar-incisor hypomineralisation
cards.take: Pooling 116 studies, this meta-analysis put the global prevalence of molar-incisor hypomineralisation (MIH) at 13.5%, and 10.7% in Asia. Affected first molars are often sensitive, break down quickly and are hard to anaesthetise. Chairside: check every first permanent molar and incisor at age 6 to 8 for chalky or yellow-brown patches, start fluoride and sealants early, and recall more often.
cards.rib: Check first molars at age 6-8 for chalky, sensitive patches

cards.head: One visit or two: root canal healing is the same
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 47 trials (5805 patients) found no difference in radiological failure at a year or more between single-visit and multiple-visit root canal treatment (RR 0.93, moderate certainty), and no clear difference in swelling, flare-ups or extractions. Single-visit patients more often reported pain within the first week (RR 1.55). Chairside: choose by time, isolation and canal control, and warn about soreness.
cards.rib: Pick visits by case control, and warn of first-week soreness

cards.head: Sensitive teeth: most desensitising pastes beat fluoride
cards.take: This network meta-analysis of 125 trials (12,541 patients) ranked desensitising toothpastes for dentine hypersensitivity. Calcium sodium phosphosilicate was most beneficial across touch, cold and air stimuli with moderate to high certainty; stannous fluoride, potassium, arginine and strontium pastes also beat regular fluoride. Chairside: rule out caries and cracks, then advise twice-daily use of a desensitising paste for several weeks.
cards.rib: Rule out caries and cracks, then prescribe a desensitising paste

cards.head: Repaired composites last as long as replaced ones
cards.take: This Dutch practice-based study followed 8542 composite restorations in 3239 patients. Failing restorations were either repaired (616) or replaced (264). Ten-year success was 43.4% after repair and 48.6% after replacement, and the authors concluded that repairs last as long as replacements while increasing overall survival. Chairside: for a chipped or partly failed composite, repair first instead of drilling it all out.
cards.rib: Repair a partly failed composite before replacing it

cards.head: Only 1 in 3 Indian chewers is advised to quit
cards.take: India's second Global Adult Tobacco Survey found 21.4% of adults (199.4 million) use smokeless tobacco. Among smokeless users who saw a health care provider in the past year, only 31.7% were advised to quit, versus 48.8% of smokers. Yet half of current chewers (49.6%) were thinking of quitting and a third had tried. Chairside: every dental visit is a chance to give that advice.
cards.rib: Give every chewer clear quit advice, even when they don't ask

fig.title: Users advised to quit by a provider

cards.ev: Policy · National Oral Health Programme, DGHS MoHFW
cards.head: NOHP has funded dental units down to PHC level
cards.take: India's National Oral Health Programme, launched in 2014-15, helps states set up dental care units in district hospitals and below, with staff, chairs, autoclaves, consumables and training. DGHS reports over 9500 units supported, including more than 5000 at primary health centres. National resource centres cover potentially malignant disorders and tobacco cessation. Chairside: know your nearest government dental unit for patients who cannot pay.
cards.rib: Map the nearest government dental unit for low-income referrals

cards.head: Dental amalgam to be phased out worldwide by 2034
cards.take: At COP-6 in Geneva in November 2025, parties to the Minamata Convention on Mercury agreed that manufacture, import and export of dental amalgam will end by 2034. An exemption allows amalgam when a dentist judges it necessary for a patient. FDI and IADR stressed prevention, affordable alternatives and proper mercury waste handling. Chairside: build prevention and adhesive skills, and fit an amalgam separator.
cards.rib: Build prevention and adhesive skills, and manage amalgam waste

cards.head: Dry mouth: no spray or gel is clearly effective
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 36 trials (1597 people) tested saliva substitutes, gels, sprays, lozenges and chewing gum for dry mouth. No topical product showed strong evidence of relieving dryness; one spray beat another by about 2 points on a 10-point scale. Sugar-free gum increased saliva when some gland function remained. Chairside: review drug causes, advise sugar-free gum and water, and add fluoride.
cards.rib: Check medicines, suggest sugar-free gum and add daily fluoride

cards.head: Early Class II treatment mainly protects the incisors
cards.take: This Cochrane review of 27 trials (1251 children) found that early two-phase treatment of prominent upper incisors with a functional appliance cut incisal trauma from 30% to 19% (OR 0.56) compared with one course in adolescence. Final overjet did not differ. Functional appliances in adolescents reduced overjet by 4.6 to 5.5 mm versus no treatment. Chairside: refer early when a large overjet is trauma-prone.
cards.rib: Refer early when a large overjet puts the incisors at risk

cards.head: 38% SDF arrested half of severe early childhood caries
cards.rib: 38% SDF arrested half of severe early childhood caries
cards.take: 830 children aged 12–71 months with severe ECC; 38% silver diamine fluoride or placebo at baseline and 6 months. Lesion arrest at 3 months: 57.5% vs 18.8%. At 8 months: 50.2% vs 17.4%. Adverse events were no more common than with placebo (47.3% vs 43.3%). Bottom line: For a child who cannot sit for restorations, twice-yearly SDF is an evidence-based way to stop cavitated lesions. Warn parents about the black staining before you apply it.

cards.head: Peri-implantitis: which antibiotic adjunct works best
cards.rib: Peri-implantitis: which antibiotic adjunct works best
cards.take: Network meta-analysis of 21 clinical studies (1,718 participants). With open-flap debridement, systemic metronidazole plus amoxicillin gave the best reduction in pocket depth and marginal bone loss. Without surgery, metronidazole alone was the best adjunct for attachment level and bone loss. Local antibiotics did less than systemic ones. Bottom line: Antibiotics support decontamination; they do not replace it. Effect sizes vary, so reserve them for confirmed peri-implantitis, not mucositis.

cards.head: Calcium silicate sealer: healing keeps improving to 5 years
cards.rib: Calcium silicate sealer: healing keeps improving to 5 years
cards.take: 637 teeth with symptomatic apical periodontitis, single operator, premixed calcium silicate sealer with cold hydraulic condensation. Strict success (no symptoms, full radiographic healing) rose from 80.2% at 1 year to 87.7% at 5 years. A larger lesion at baseline (higher PAI score) was the strongest predictor of incomplete healing. Sealer extrusion did not affect outcome. Bottom line: A lesion that is smaller but not gone at one year is often still healing. Keep reviewing before you plan a retreatment or surgery.

cards.head: Root canals work as well in autoimmune disease
cards.rib: Root canals work as well in autoimmune disease
cards.take: 203 patients with autoimmune disease (317 teeth) matched with 203 controls (312 teeth), followed for about four years. Success rates did not differ between groups. The inflammatory bowel disease subgroup did worse than rheumatoid arthritis or psoriasis. Tooth type, arch and a preoperative periapical lesion predicted outcome. Autoimmune disease did not. Bottom line: An autoimmune diagnosis is not a reason to choose extraction over endodontics. Local factors decide the prognosis.

cards.ev: In vitro study · The Open Dentistry Journal 2026
cards.head: Endocrown or post and crown for a root-treated incisor
cards.rib: Endocrown or post and crown for a root-treated incisor
cards.take: 20 extracted maxillary central incisors loaded at 45° until failure. Fracture resistance did not differ significantly between the two designs. 80% of endocrown failures were repairable, compared with 60% for post-and-core. Bottom line: A lab study of 20 teeth, without thermal cycling or fatigue. The endocrown looks promising for anterior teeth, but clinical data are still needed.

cards.ev: Clinical trial · J Pharmacy & Bioallied Sciences Dec 2025
cards.head: Loupes cut root canal time and errors
cards.rib: Loupes cut root canal time and errors
cards.take: 100 patients: root canal treatment with magnifying loupes or without. Treatment time was about 25% shorter with loupes. Procedural errors were significantly fewer (P < 0.05), and patients were more satisfied. Bottom line: Loupes are an inexpensive upgrade with a measurable effect. The trial is small and its randomisation is not described, so treat the size of the effect with caution.

cards.ev: Systematic review · Clinical and Experimental Dental Research 2026
cards.head: Clear aligners are kinder to the gingiva
cards.rib: Clear aligners are kinder to the gingiva
cards.take: Systematic review of 12 studies. From one month to one year, aligner patients had less plaque, less gingival inflammation and shallower pockets. S. mutans counts were consistently lower with aligners. Bottom line: For a patient with periodontal risk, aligners make hygiene easier, mainly because they come out. Fixed-appliance patients need closer hygiene review.

cards.ev: Systematic review and meta-analysis · BMC Oral Health 2026
cards.head: LIPUS in orthodontics: not ready for routine use
cards.rib: LIPUS in orthodontics: not ready for routine use
cards.take: Meta-analysis of 11 studies of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound. Pain at 24 hours: no significant difference from controls (MD −0.76; 95% CI −2.86 to 1.33). Results on faster tooth movement ranged from substantial to negligible. Bottom line: Do not sell LIPUS to patients as faster or painless treatment yet. Standardised RCTs are needed.

cards.head: Severe periodontitis tracks with diabetic retinal change
cards.rib: Severe periodontitis tracks with diabetic retinal change
cards.take: 100 participants, from healthy controls to proliferative diabetic retinopathy, examined with OCT and OCT-angiography. Stage III–IV periodontitis was associated with thinner retinal nerve fibre layers and lower retinal vessel density. The design is cross-sectional, so it shows association, not cause. Bottom line: For a diabetic patient with advanced periodontitis, treat the gums and ask whether their yearly retinal check is up to date.

cards.ev: Lodi G et al. · Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2021
cards.head: Antibiotics at extraction: what they buy, what they cost
cards.rib: Antibiotics at extraction: what they buy, what they cost
cards.take: Cochrane review, mostly third molar surgery in healthy adults. Antibiotics reduced postoperative infection by about two-thirds (NNT 19) and dry socket by about a third (NNT 46). Adverse effects were mostly brief and minor, but each prescription adds to resistance. Bottom line: Treating 19 healthy patients to prevent one infection is a poor trade for routine extractions. Reserve antibiotics for higher-risk patients and difficult surgery.

cards.head: Acute dental pain: NSAIDs first, opioids last
cards.rib: Acute dental pain: NSAIDs first, opioids last
cards.take: ADA guideline for adolescents (12 and over) and adults. NSAIDs alone, or combined with paracetamol (acetaminophen), are the first choice for pain after extraction and for toothache. Opioids are reserved for the rare case where these fail or are contraindicated. Bottom line: Ibuprofen with paracetamol relieves dental pain as well as opioid combinations, without the dependence risk.

cards.head: Toothache needs treatment, not an antibiotic
cards.rib: Toothache needs treatment, not an antibiotic
cards.take: ADA guideline for immunocompetent adults. No antibiotics for symptomatic irreversible pulpitis, or for pulp necrosis with apical periodontitis or a localised abscess. Antibiotics are for systemic involvement (fever, malaise, spreading swelling, lymphadenopathy) or when definitive treatment cannot be done. Bottom line: Pulpectomy, incision and drainage or extraction is the treatment. An antibiotic without them only delays it.

cards.head: Endocarditis prophylaxis: who still needs it
cards.rib: Endocarditis prophylaxis: who still needs it
cards.take: Only the highest-risk patients: prosthetic valves or valve repair material, previous endocarditis, certain congenital heart disease, and cardiac transplant with valvulopathy. Only for procedures that manipulate the gingiva or periapical region, or perforate the mucosa. Amoxicillin 2 g orally, 30–60 minutes before. Clindamycin is no longer recommended. Bottom line: Rheumatic heart disease without a prosthetic valve, mitral valve prolapse or a stent does not need prophylaxis under this guidance. When unsure, ask the cardiologist.

cards.ev: Sanz M et al. · J Clin Periodontol 2020
cards.head: The EFP four-step treatment of periodontitis
cards.rib: The EFP four-step treatment of periodontitis
cards.take: Step 1: oral hygiene instruction, risk factor control (stop smoking, control diabetes) and supragingival cleaning. Step 2: subgingival instrumentation. Systemic antibiotics are not routine; consider them only in specific young patients with severe disease. Step 3: re-evaluate, then treat residual pockets (4 mm or deeper with bleeding, or 6 mm or deeper). Step 4: supportive care every 3–12 months. Bottom line: The re-evaluation visit is what most practices skip. Book it before the patient leaves after step 2.

cards.head: Edentulous mandible: two implants make the denture
cards.rib: Edentulous mandible: two implants make the denture
cards.take: The McGill consensus statement made the two-implant overdenture the minimum standard of care for the edentulous mandible. It gives better retention, chewing and satisfaction than a conventional complete denture. Two implants cost far less than a fixed full-arch prosthesis. Bottom line: Offer it to every patient struggling with a lower denture. It is often the most cost-effective implant treatment in the practice.

cards.ev: Ruggiero SL et al. · J Oral Maxillofac Surg 2022
cards.head: Extraction in a patient on bisphosphonates
cards.rib: Extraction in a patient on bisphosphonates
cards.take: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is far less common at osteoporosis doses than at the doses used for cancer. Before starting cancer-dose antiresorptives, complete dental treatment and let extraction sites heal. Evidence for stopping the drug before extraction (a 'drug holiday') remains limited. Talk to the prescribing physician. Bottom line: Do not refuse a needed extraction to an osteoporosis patient. Extract atraumatically, close primarily where possible, and review healing.

cards.head: National Dental Commission replaces the DCI
cards.rib: National Dental Commission replaces the DCI
cards.take: The National Dental Commission Act, 2023 was notified in March 2026. Dental graduates will have to pass the National Exit Test (NExT) to practise. It is to be introduced within three years. State dental council heads will now be appointed by state governments, and the Commission can regulate fees for half the seats in private colleges. Bottom line: Registered practitioners keep their registration. Watch for the NExT schedule if you teach or employ new graduates.
